Proverbs 1:2.title: Proverbs 1:2
Proverbs 1:2.content: To know … instruction—literally, "for knowing," that is, such is the design of these writings. wisdom—or the use of the best means for the best ends, is generally employed in this book for true piety. instruction—discipline, by which men are trained. to perceive—literally, "for perceiving," the design (as above) understanding—that is, words which enable one to discern good and evil.

Proverbs 1:3.title: Proverbs 1:3
Proverbs 1:3.content: To receive … of wisdom—For receiving that discipline which discretion imparts. The Hebrew for "wisdom" differs from that of Pr 1:2, and denotes rather discreet counsel. Compare the opposite traits of the fool (Pr 16:22). justice … equity—all the attributes of one upright in all his relations to God and man.

Proverbs 1:4.title: Proverbs 1:4
Proverbs 1:4.content: simple—one easily led to good or evil; so the parallel. young man—one inexperienced. subtilty—or prudence (Pr 3:21; 5:21). discretion—literally, "device," both qualities, either good or bad, according to their use. Here good, as they imply wariness by which to escape evil and find good.

Proverbs 1:5.title: Proverbs 1:5-6
Proverbs 1:5.content: Such writings the wise, who pursue right ends by right means, will value. learning—not the act, but matter of it. wise counsels—or the art and principles of governing.

Proverbs 8:7.title: Proverbs 8:7
Proverbs 8:7.content: For … truth—literally, "My palate shall meditate," or (as Orientals did) "mutter," my thoughts expressed only to myself are truth. wickedness—specially falsehood, as opposed to truth.

Proverbs 8:8.title: Proverbs 8:8
Proverbs 8:8.content: in righteousness—or, "righteous" (Ps 9:8,11:7). froward—literally, "twisted," or contradictory, that is, to truth.

Proverbs 8:9.title: Proverbs 8:9
Proverbs 8:9.content: plain … understandeth—easily seen by those who apply their minds. that find—implying search.

Proverbs 8:10.title: Proverbs 8:10
Proverbs 8:10.content: not silver—preferable to it, so last clause implies comparison.

Proverbs 8:12.title: Proverbs 8:12
Proverbs 8:12.content: prudence—as in Pr 8:5. The connection of "wisdom" and "prudence" is that of the dictates of sound wisdom and its application. find … inventions—or, "devices," "discreet ways" (Pr 1:4).

Proverbs 8:13.title: Proverbs 8:13
Proverbs 8:13.content: For such is the effect of the fear of God, by which hatred to evil preserves from it. froward mouth—or, "speech" (Pr 2:12; 6:14).

Proverbs 8:14.title: Proverbs 8:14
Proverbs 8:14.content: It also gives the elements of good character in counsel. sound wisdom—(Pr 2:7). I … strength—or, "As for me, understanding is strength to me," the source of power (Ec 9:16); good judgment gives more efficiency to actions;

Proverbs 8:15.content: of which a wisely conducted government is an example.

Proverbs 8:16.content: of which a wisely conducted government is an example.

Proverbs 8:17.content: early—or, "diligently," which may include the usual sense of early in life.

Proverbs 8:18.title: Proverbs 8:18
Proverbs 8:18.content: durable riches … righteousness—Such are the "riches," enduring sources of happiness in moral possessions (compare Pr 3:16).

Proverbs 8:20.title: Proverbs 8:20-21
Proverbs 8:20.content: The courses in which wisdom leads conduct to a true present prosperity (Pr 23:5).

Proverbs 8:22.title: Proverbs 8:22-31
Proverbs 8:22.content: Strictly, God's attributes are part of Himself. Yet, to the poetical structure of the whole passage, this commendation of wisdom is entirely consonant. In order of time all His attributes are coincident and eternal as Himself. But to set forth the importance of wisdom as devising the products of benevolence and power, it is here assigned a precedence. As it has such in divine, so should it be desired in human, affairs (compare Pr 3:19). possessed—or, "created"; in either sense, the idea of precedence. in the beginning—or simply, "beginning," in apposition with "me." before … of old—preceding the most ancient deeds.

Proverbs 9:1.title: Proverbs 9:1
Proverbs 9:1.content: house—(compare Pr 8:34). her—or, "its" (the house). seven pillars—the number seven for many, or a sufficiency (Pr 6:31).

Proverbs 9:2.title: Proverbs 9:2
Proverbs 9:2.content: mingled—to enhance the flavor (Pr 23:30; Isa 5:22). furnished—literally, "set out," "arranged."

Proverbs 9:3.title: Proverbs 9:3
Proverbs 9:3.content: maidens—servants to invite (compare Ps 68:11; Isa 40:9). highest places—ridges of heights, conspicuous places.

Proverbs 9:4.content: (Compare Pr 1:4; 6:32). Wisdom not only supplies right but forbids wrong principles.

Proverbs 9:7.content: shame—(Compare Pr 3:35). a blot—or, "stain on character." Both terms denote the evil done by others to one whose faithfulness secures a wise man's love.

Proverbs 9:8.content: shame—(Compare Pr 3:35). a blot—or, "stain on character." Both terms denote the evil done by others to one whose faithfulness secures a wise man's love.

Proverbs 9:9.title: Proverbs 9:9
Proverbs 9:9.content: The more a wise man learns, the more he loves wisdom.

Proverbs 9:10.title: Proverbs 9:10
Proverbs 9:10.content: (Compare Pr 1:7). of the holy—literally, "holies," persons or things, or both. This knowledge gives right perception.

Proverbs 9:12.title: Proverbs 9:12
Proverbs 9:12.content: You are mainly concerned in your own conduct.

Proverbs 9:13.title: Proverbs 9:13
Proverbs 9:13.content: foolish woman—or literally, "woman of folly," specially manifested by such as are described. clamorous—or, "noisy" (Pr 7:11). knoweth nothing—literally, "knoweth not what," that is, is right and proper.

Proverbs 9:14.title: Proverbs 9:14
Proverbs 9:14.content: on a seat—literally, "throne," takes a prominent place, impudently and haughtily.

Proverbs 9:15.title: Proverbs 9:15-16
Proverbs 9:15.content: to allure those who are right-minded, and who are addressed as in Pr 9:4, as simple—that is, easily led (Pr 1:4) and unsettled, though willing to do right.

Proverbs 9:16.title: Proverbs 9:15-16
Proverbs 9:16.content: to allure those who are right-minded, and who are addressed as in Pr 9:4, as simple—that is, easily led (Pr 1:4) and unsettled, though willing to do right.

Proverbs 9:17.title: Proverbs 9:17
Proverbs 9:17.content: The language of a proverb, meaning that forbidden delights are sweet and pleasant, as fruits of risk and danger.

Proverbs 10:1.title: Proverbs 10:1
Proverbs 10:1.content: wise [and] foolish—as they follow or reject the precepts of wisdom. maketh … father—or, "gladdens a father." heaviness—or, "grief."

Proverbs 10:2.title: Proverbs 10:2
Proverbs 10:2.content: Treasures … nothing—that is, Ill-gotten gains give no true happiness (compare Pr 4:17; Mt 6:19). righteousness—especially beneficence (Ps 112:9). death—the greatest of all evils.

Proverbs 10:3.title: Proverbs 10:3
Proverbs 10:3.content: (Compare Ps 37:16-20). The last clause is better: "He will repel the greedy desires of the wicked."

Proverbs 10:4.title: Proverbs 10:4
Proverbs 10:4.content: slack—literally, "deceitful," failing of its purpose (compare Ho 7:16). maketh rich—(compare Pr 10:22).

Proverbs 10:5.title: Proverbs 10:5
Proverbs 10:5.content: son—as Pr 1:8, 10, and often. sleepeth—in indolence, and not for rest. causeth shame—literally, "is base" (compare Pr 14:35; 17:2).

Proverbs 10:6.title: Proverbs 10:6
Proverbs 10:6.content: Blessings—literally, "Praises." The last clause is better: "The mouth of the wicked covereth (or concealeth) violence (or mischievous devices)" to be executed in due time (Ps 5:9; 10:7; Ro 3:14), and hence has no praises (compare Pr 10:11).

Proverbs 10:7.title: Proverbs 10:7
Proverbs 10:7.content: blessed—literally, "for a blessing," or praise. shall rot—literally, "be worm-eaten," useless and disgusting.

Proverbs 10:8.title: Proverbs 10:8
Proverbs 10:8.content: wise, &c.—(compare Pr 9:8, 9, 16), opposed to prating fool—or, "fool of lips of wicked language." fall—headlong, suddenly.

Proverbs 10:9.title: Proverbs 10:9
Proverbs 10:9.content: perverteth his ways—acts deceitfully. known—discovered and punished.

Proverbs 10:10.title: Proverbs 10:10
Proverbs 10:10.content: Two vices contrasted; hypocrisy, or insinuating evil against one (Pr 6:13; Ps 35:19), and rashness of speech. In each case, the results are on the evildoers.

Proverbs 10:11.title: Proverbs 10:11
Proverbs 10:11.content: a well—or, "source" of good to himself and others (Joh 7:37, 38). On last clause, see on Pr 10:6.

Proverbs 10:13.title: Proverbs 10:13
Proverbs 10:13.content: In the lips … found—hence, not beaten, as the wicked-speaking fool. void of understanding—(Pr 6:32; 7:7).

Proverbs 10:14.title: Proverbs 10:14
Proverbs 10:14.content: lay up knowledge—that is, as treasures for good use. mouth … destruction—or, "as to the mouth," &c., destruction is near; they expose themselves to evil by prating.

Proverbs 10:15.title: Proverbs 10:15
Proverbs 10:15.content: Both by trusting in "uncertain riches" (1Ti 6:17), or by the evils of poverty (Pr 30:9), men, not fearing God, fall into dangers.

Proverbs 10:16.title: Proverbs 10:16
Proverbs 10:16.content: The industry of the righteous is alone truly successful, while the earnings of the wicked tempt and lead to sin.

Proverbs 10:17.title: Proverbs 10:17
Proverbs 10:17.content: keepeth—observes (Pr 3:18; 4:22). refuseth—or, "turns from reproof," which might direct him aright.

Proverbs 10:18.title: Proverbs 10:18
Proverbs 10:18.content: Both vices must one day be known and punished, and hence their folly.

Proverbs 10:19.title: Proverbs 10:19
Proverbs 10:19.content: Much speech involves risk of sin; hence the wisdom of restraining the tongue (Ps 39:1; Jas 1:26).

Proverbs 10:20.title: Proverbs 10:20
Proverbs 10:20.content: Right speech is the fruit of a good heart, but the wicked show theirs to be useless.

Proverbs 10:21.title: Proverbs 10:21
Proverbs 10:21.content: Fools not only fail to benefit others, as do the righteous, but procure their own ruin (compare Pr 10:11, 17; Ho 4:6).

Proverbs 10:22.title: Proverbs 10:22
Proverbs 10:22.content: it maketh, &c.—"it" is emphatic. Riches from God are without the sorrow of ill-gotten wealth (compare Ec 2:21-23; 1Ti 6:9, 10, 17).

Proverbs 10:23.title: Proverbs 10:23
Proverbs 10:23.content: Sin is the pleasure of the wicked; wisdom that of the good.

Proverbs 10:24.title: Proverbs 10:24
Proverbs 10:24.content: it—the very thing. The wicked get dreaded evil; the righteous, desired good.

Proverbs 10:25.title: Proverbs 10:25
Proverbs 10:25.content: (Compare Ps 1:4; 37:9, 10, 36). righteous … foundation—well laid and firm (Mt 7:24, 25).

Proverbs 10:28.title: Proverbs 10:28
Proverbs 10:28.content: gladness—in confidence of realizing it. expectation … perish—in disappointment.

Proverbs 10:29.title: Proverbs 10:29
Proverbs 10:29.content: The way, &c.—that is, God's providence sustains the righteous and overthrows the wicked (Ho 14:9).

Proverbs 10:31.title: Proverbs 10:31
Proverbs 10:31.content: bringeth forth—literally, "germinates" as a plant. froward—(Compare Pr 2:12, 14). cut off—as an unproductive plant.

Proverbs 10:32.title: Proverbs 10:32
Proverbs 10:32.content: know—regard and provide for (Ps 1:6). frowardness—all kinds of deceit and ill-nature. The word is plural.

Proverbs 11:1.title: Proverbs 11:1
Proverbs 11:1.content: (Compare Margin). The Hebrews used stones for weights. just—complete in measure.

Proverbs 11:2.title: Proverbs 11:2
Proverbs 11:2.content: Self-conceit is unteachable; the humble grow wise (compare Pr 16:18; 18:12).

Proverbs 11:3.title: Proverbs 11:3
Proverbs 11:3.content: guide—to lead, as a shepherd (Pr 6:7; Ps 78:52). perverseness—ill-nature. destroy—with violence.

Proverbs 11:5.title: Proverbs 11:5
Proverbs 11:5.content: direct—or, "make plain"; wicked ways are not plain (Pr 13:17).

Proverbs 11:6.title: Proverbs 11:6
Proverbs 11:6.content: deliver them—that is, from evil, which the wicked suffer by their own doings (Pr 5:22; Ps 9:16).

Proverbs 11:7.title: Proverbs 11:7
Proverbs 11:7.content: expectation … perish—for death cuts short all his plans (Lu 16:25). hope of unjust—better, "hope of wealth," or "power" (compare Isa 40:29, Hebrew). This gives an advance on the sentiment of the first clause. Even hopes of gain die with him.

Proverbs 11:8.title: Proverbs 11:8
Proverbs 11:8.content: Perhaps the trouble prepared by the wicked, and which he inherits (compare Pr 11:6).

Proverbs 11:9.title: Proverbs 11:9
Proverbs 11:9.content: (Compare Ps 35:16; Da 11:32). The just is saved by superior discernment.

Proverbs 11:10.title: Proverbs 11:10-11
Proverbs 11:10.content: The last may be a reason for the first. Together, they set forth the relative moral worth of good and bad men.

Proverbs 11:11.title: Proverbs 11:10-11
Proverbs 11:11.content: The last may be a reason for the first. Together, they set forth the relative moral worth of good and bad men.

Proverbs 11:12.title: Proverbs 11:12
Proverbs 11:12.content: despiseth—or, "reviles," a course contrasted with the prudent silence of the wise. holdeth his peace—as if neither hearing nor telling.

Proverbs 11:13.title: Proverbs 11:13
Proverbs 11:13.content: tale-bearer—(Compare Margin), one trading as a peddler in scandal, whose propensity to talk leads him to betray confidence.

Proverbs 11:14.title: Proverbs 11:14
Proverbs 11:14.content: counsel—the art of governing (Pr 1:5). counsellors—literally, "one giving counsel"; the participle used as a collective.

Proverbs 11:15.title: Proverbs 11:15
Proverbs 11:15.content: (Compare Pr 6:1). suretiship—(Compare Margin), the actors put for the action, which may be lawfully hated.

Proverbs 11:16.title: Proverbs 11:16
Proverbs 11:16.content: retaineth—or literally, "lay hold of as a support." Honor is to a feeble woman thus as valuable as riches to men.

Proverbs 11:17.title: Proverbs 11:17
Proverbs 11:17.content: merciful—kind to others; opposed to cruel. Such benefit themselves by doing good to others (compare Pr 24:5), while the cruel injure themselves as well as others. flesh—that is, his body, by penuriousness (Col 2:23).

Proverbs 11:18.title: Proverbs 11:18
Proverbs 11:18.content: a deceitful work—or, "wages," which fail to satisfy, or flee away (Pr 10:2; 23:5). sure reward—or, "gain," as from trading (Ho 10:12; Ga 6:8, 9).

Proverbs 11:20.title: Proverbs 11:20
Proverbs 11:20.content: (Compare Pr 11:5). froward—as in Pr 2:15, opposed to the simplicity and purity of the upright. in their way—or, "conduct."

Proverbs 11:21.title: Proverbs 11:21
Proverbs 11:21.content: The combined power of the wicked cannot free them from just punishment, while the unaided children of the righteous find deliverance by reason of their pious relationship (Ps 37:25, 26).

Proverbs 11:22.title: Proverbs 11:22
Proverbs 11:22.content: Jewels were often suspended from the nose (Ge 24:47; Isa 3:21). Thus adorned, a hog disgusts less than a fair and indiscreet woman.

Proverbs 11:24.title: Proverbs 11:24-31
Proverbs 11:24.content: The scope of the whole is a comment on Pr 11:23. Thus liberality, by God's blessing, secures increase, while penuriousness, instead of expected gain, procures poverty.

Proverbs 11:25.content: The scope of the whole is a comment on Pr 11:23. Thus liberality, by God's blessing, secures increase, while penuriousness, instead of expected gain, procures poverty.

Proverbs 11:25.title: Proverbs 11:25
Proverbs 11:25.content: liberal soul—(Compare Margin). made fat—prospers (Pr 28:25; De 32:15; Lu 6:38). watereth … watered—a common figure for blessing.

Proverbs 11:26.title: Proverbs 11:24-31
Proverbs 11:26.content: The scope of the whole is a comment on Pr 11:23. Thus liberality, by God's blessing, secures increase, while penuriousness, instead of expected gain, procures poverty.

Proverbs 11:26.title: Proverbs 11:26
Proverbs 11:26.content: Another example of the truth of Pr 11:23; the miser loses reputation, though he saves corn. selleth it—that is, at a fair price.

Proverbs 11:27.title: Proverbs 11:24-31
Proverbs 11:27.content: The scope of the whole is a comment on Pr 11:23. Thus liberality, by God's blessing, secures increase, while penuriousness, instead of expected gain, procures poverty.

Proverbs 11:27.title: Proverbs 11:27
Proverbs 11:27.content: good [and] mischief—that is, of others. procureth … seeketh—implying success.

Proverbs 11:28.title: Proverbs 11:24-31
Proverbs 11:28.content: The scope of the whole is a comment on Pr 11:23. Thus liberality, by God's blessing, secures increase, while penuriousness, instead of expected gain, procures poverty.

Proverbs 11:29.title: Proverbs 11:24-31
Proverbs 11:29.content: The scope of the whole is a comment on Pr 11:23. Thus liberality, by God's blessing, secures increase, while penuriousness, instead of expected gain, procures poverty.

Proverbs 11:29.title: Proverbs 11:29
Proverbs 11:29.content: troubleth—as Pr 15:27 explains, by greediness for gain (compare Pr 11:17). inherit … wind—Even successful, his gains are of no real value. So the fool, thus acting, either comes to poverty, or heaps up for others.

Proverbs 11:30.title: Proverbs 11:24-31
Proverbs 11:30.content: The scope of the whole is a comment on Pr 11:23. Thus liberality, by God's blessing, secures increase, while penuriousness, instead of expected gain, procures poverty.

Proverbs 11:30.title: Proverbs 11:30
Proverbs 11:30.content: a tree of life—Blessings to others proceed from the works of the righteous (Pr 3:18). winneth souls—(Compare Margin) to do them good as opposed to Pr 6:25; Eze 13:18 (compare Lu 5:10).

Proverbs 11:31.title: Proverbs 11:24-31
Proverbs 11:31.content: The scope of the whole is a comment on Pr 11:23. Thus liberality, by God's blessing, secures increase, while penuriousness, instead of expected gain, procures poverty.

Proverbs 11:31.title: Proverbs 11:31
Proverbs 11:31.content: Behold—Thus calling attention to the illustrations (compare Pr 11:23), the sentiment of which is confirmed even in time, not excluding future rewards and punishments.

Proverbs 12:1.title: Proverbs 12:1
Proverbs 12:1.content: loveth knowledge—as the fruit of instruction or training (Pr 1:2). hateth reproof—(Pr 10:17). brutish—stupid, regardless of his own welfare (Ps 49:10; 73:22).

Proverbs 12:3.title: Proverbs 12:3
Proverbs 12:3.content: Wickedness cannot give permanent prosperity. root … not be moved—firm as a flourishing tree—(Ps 1:3; 15:5; Jer 17:8).

Proverbs 12:4.title: Proverbs 12:4
Proverbs 12:4.content: A virtuous woman—in the wide sense of well-disposed to all moral duties (Pr 31:10). maketh ashamed—that is, by misconduct. rottenness—an incurable evil.

Proverbs 12:5.title: Proverbs 12:5
Proverbs 12:5.content: thoughts—or, "purposes." are right—literally, "are judgment," that is, true decisions. counsels—(Compare Pr 11:14). deceit—contrary to truth and honesty.

Proverbs 12:6.title: Proverbs 12:6
Proverbs 12:6.content: The words—or, "expressed designs" of the wicked are for evil purposes. the mouth—or, "words" of the righteous delivering instead of ensnaring men.

Proverbs 12:7.title: Proverbs 12:7
Proverbs 12:7.content: Such conduct brings a proper return, by the destruction of the wicked and well-being of the righteous and his family.

Proverbs 12:8.title: Proverbs 12:8
Proverbs 12:8.content: despised—as opposed to commended (Pr 11:12). perverse heart—or, "wicked principles," as opposed to one of wisdom.

Proverbs 12:9.title: Proverbs 12:9
Proverbs 12:9.content: despised—held in little repute, obscure (1Sa 18:23; Isa 3:5). hath a servant—implying some means of honest living. honoureth himself—is self-conceited.

Proverbs 12:10.title: Proverbs 12:10
Proverbs 12:10.content: regardeth—literally, "knoweth" (Ps 1:6). mercies … cruel—as acts of compassion ungraciously rendered to the needy. The righteous more regards a beast than the wicked a man.

Proverbs 12:11.title: Proverbs 12:11
Proverbs 12:11.content: The idler's fate is the result of indolence and want of principle (Pr 6:32; 7:7).

Proverbs 12:12.title: Proverbs 12:12
Proverbs 12:12.content: the wicked … evil—They love the crafty arts of deception. the root … fruit—their own resources supply them; or, it may be rendered: "He (God) giveth, or, sets (Eze 17:22) the root of the righteous," and hence it is firm: or, the verb is impersonal; "As to the root … it is firm" (Pr 17:19).

Proverbs 12:13.title: Proverbs 12:13-14
Proverbs 12:13.content: The wicked is snared, &c.—The sentiment expanded. While the wicked, such as liars, flatterers, &c., fall by their own words, the righteous are unhurt. Their good conduct makes friends, and God rewards them.

Proverbs 12:14.title: Proverbs 12:13-14
Proverbs 12:14.content: The wicked is snared, &c.—The sentiment expanded. While the wicked, such as liars, flatterers, &c., fall by their own words, the righteous are unhurt. Their good conduct makes friends, and God rewards them.

Proverbs 12:15.title: Proverbs 12:15
Proverbs 12:15.content: The way … eyes—The fool is self-conceited (compare Pr 12:1; 1:32; 10:17; Jas 3:17).

Proverbs 12:16.title: Proverbs 12:16
Proverbs 12:16.content: prudent … shame—He is slow to denounce his insulters (Jas 1:19).

Proverbs 12:18.title: Proverbs 12:18
Proverbs 12:18.content: speaketh—literally, "speaketh hastily," or indiscreetly (Ps 106:33), as an angry man retorts harsh and provoking invectives. tongue … health—by soothing and gentle language.

Proverbs 12:19.title: Proverbs 12:19
Proverbs 12:19.content: Words of truth are consistent, and stand all tests, while lies are soon discovered and exposed.

Proverbs 12:20.title: Proverbs 12:20
Proverbs 12:20.content: that imagine—or, "plan" (Pr 3:29). They design a deceitful course, to which, with all its evils and dangers to others and themselves, the happiness of peace-makers is opposed (compare Mt 5:9; Ro 12:18).

Proverbs 12:21.title: Proverbs 12:21
Proverbs 12:21.content: no evil—(as in Ps 91:10), under God's wise limitations (Ro 8:28). mischief—as penal evil.

Proverbs 12:22.title: Proverbs 12:22
Proverbs 12:22.content: deal truly—or, "faithfully," that is, according to promises (compare Joh 3:21).

Proverbs 12:23.title: Proverbs 12:23
Proverbs 12:23.content: concealeth—by his modesty (Pr 10:14; 11:13). heart … proclaimeth—as his lips speak his thoughts (compare Ec 10:3).

Proverbs 12:24.title: Proverbs 12:24
Proverbs 12:24.content: slothful—(Compare Margin), so called because he fails to meet his promises. under tribute—not denoting legal taxes, but the obligation of dependence.

Proverbs 12:26.title: Proverbs 12:26
Proverbs 12:26.content: more excellent—(Compare Margin); or, "more successful," while the wicked fail; or, we may read it: "The righteous guides his friend, but," &c., that is, The ability of the righteous to aid others is contrasted with the ruin to which the way of the wicked leads themselves.

Proverbs 12:27.title: Proverbs 12:27
Proverbs 12:27.content: (Compare Pr 12:24). took in hunting—or, "his venison." He does not improve his advantages. the substance … precious—or, "the wealth of a man of honor is being diligent," or "diligence." precious—literally, "honor" (Ec 10:1).

Proverbs 12:28.title: Proverbs 12:28
Proverbs 12:28.content: (Compare Pr 8:8, 20, &c.). A sentiment often stated; here first affirmatively, then negatively.

Proverbs 13:2.title: Proverbs 13:2
Proverbs 13:2.content: shall eat—that is, obtain (Pr 12:14). transgressors—as in Pr 2:22. violence—or, "mischief" to themselves.

Proverbs 13:3.title: Proverbs 13:3
Proverbs 13:3.content: He … mouth … life—because evil speeches may provoke violence from others. he that openeth wide his lips shall have destruction—On last clause, compare Pr 10:14.

Proverbs 13:5.title: Proverbs 13:5
Proverbs 13:5.content: loathsome … shame—better, causeth shame and reproach (compare Pr 19:26), by slander, &c., which the righteous hates.

Proverbs 13:6.title: Proverbs 13:6
Proverbs 13:6.content: A sentiment of frequent recurrence, that piety benefits and sin injures.

Proverbs 13:7.title: Proverbs 13:7
Proverbs 13:7.content: In opposite ways men act hypocritically for gain of honor or wealth.

Proverbs 13:8.title: Proverbs 13:8
Proverbs 13:8.content: Riches save some from punishment, while others suffer because they will not heed the rebuke of sloth, which makes and keeps them poor.

Proverbs 13:9.title: Proverbs 13:9
Proverbs 13:9.content: light … lamp—prosperity; the first, the greater, and it rejoiceth—burns brightly, or continues, while the other, at best small, soon fails.

Proverbs 13:10.title: Proverbs 13:10
Proverbs 13:10.content: The obstinacy which attends self-conceit, produces contention, which the well-advised, thus evincing modesty, avoid.

Proverbs 13:11.title: Proverbs 13:11
Proverbs 13:11.content: by vanity—or, "nothingness," that is, which is vain or useless to the public (as card playing or similar vices). gathereth … labour—(Compare Margin), little by little, laboriously.

Proverbs 13:12.title: Proverbs 13:12
Proverbs 13:12.content: desire cometh—is realized. a tree of life—or, "cause of happiness."

Proverbs 13:13.title: Proverbs 13:13
Proverbs 13:13.content: the word—that is, of advice, or, instruction (compare Pr 10:27; 11:31).

Proverbs 13:14.title: Proverbs 13:14
Proverbs 13:14.content: (Compare Pr 10:11). fountain—or, "source of life." to depart—(compare Pr 1:2-4), or, "for departing," &c., and so gives life.

Proverbs 13:15.title: Proverbs 13:15
Proverbs 13:15.content: Right perception and action secure good will, while evil ways are difficult as a stony road. The wicked left of God find punishment of sin in sinning. hard—or, "harsh" (compare Hebrew: De 21:4; Jer 5:15).

Proverbs 13:16.title: Proverbs 13:16
Proverbs 13:16.content: dealeth—acts with foresight. a fool … folly—for want of caution.

Proverbs 13:17.title: Proverbs 13:17
Proverbs 13:17.content: A wicked—or, "unfaithful" messenger falleth into mischief—or, "by mischief," or "evil," and so his errand fails. Contrasted is the character of the faithful, whose faithfulness benefits others.

Proverbs 13:19.title: Proverbs 13:19
Proverbs 13:19.content: Self-denial, which fools will not endure, is essential to success.

Proverbs 13:20.title: Proverbs 13:20
Proverbs 13:20.content: The benefits of good and evil of bad society are contrasted.

Proverbs 13:21.title: Proverbs 13:21
Proverbs 13:21.content: (Compare Pr 11:31). good … repaid—or, "He (God) will repay good."

Proverbs 13:22.title: Proverbs 13:22
Proverbs 13:22.content: wealth … just—While good men's estates remain in their families, God so orders that the gains of sinners enure to the just (compare Pr 28:8; Ps 37:18, 22, 26, &c.).

Proverbs 13:23.title: Proverbs 13:23
Proverbs 13:23.content: The laboring poor prosper more than those who injudiciously or wickedly strive, by fraud and violence, to supersede the necessity of lawful labor.

Proverbs 13:24.title: Proverbs 13:24
Proverbs 13:24.content: spareth—or, "withholds." rod—of correction. hateth—or, acts as if he hated him (compare Pr 3:12; 8:36). chasteneth … betimes—or, "diligently seeks for him all useful discipline."

Proverbs 13:25.title: Proverbs 13:25
Proverbs 13:25.content: The comparative temporal prosperity of the righteous and wicked, rather than contentment and discontent, is noted.

Proverbs 14:1.title: Proverbs 14:1
Proverbs 14:1.content: Every wise, &c.—literally, "The wisdoms" (compare Pr 9:1) "of women," plural, a distributive form of speech. buildeth … house—increases wealth, which the foolish, by mismanagement, lessen.

Proverbs 14:2.title: Proverbs 14:2
Proverbs 14:2.content: uprightness—is the fruit of fearing God, as falsehood and ill-nature (Pr 2:15; 3:32) of despising Him and His law.

Proverbs 14:3.title: Proverbs 14:3
Proverbs 14:3.content: rod of pride—that is, the punishment of pride, which they evince by their words. The words of the wise procure good to them.

Proverbs 14:4.title: Proverbs 14:4
Proverbs 14:4.content: crib is clean—empty; so "cleanness of teeth" denotes want of food (compare Am 4:6). Men get the proper fruit of their doings (Ga 6:7).

Proverbs 14:5.title: Proverbs 14:5
Proverbs 14:5.content: A faithful witness, &c.—one tested to be such. utter lies—or, "breathe out lies"—that is, habitually lies (Pr 6:19; compare Ac 9:1). Or the sense is, that habitual truthfulness, or lying, will be evinced in witness-bearing.

Proverbs 14:6.title: Proverbs 14:6
Proverbs 14:6.content: An humble, teachable spirit succeeds in seeking (Pr 8:9; Joh 7:17; Jas 1:5, 6).

Proverbs 14:7.title: Proverbs 14:7
Proverbs 14:7.content: Avoid the society of those who cannot teach you.

Proverbs 14:8.title: Proverbs 14:8
Proverbs 14:8.content: Appearances deceive the thoughtless, but the prudent discriminate.

Proverbs 14:9.title: Proverbs 14:9
Proverbs 14:9.content: Fools make a mock at sin—or, "Sin deludes fools." righteous … favour—that is, of God, instead of the punishment of sin.

Proverbs 14:10.title: Proverbs 14:10
Proverbs 14:10.content: Each one best knows his own sorrows or joys.

Proverbs 14:11.title: Proverbs 14:11
Proverbs 14:11.content: (Compare Pr 12:7). The contrast of the whole is enhanced by that of house and tabernacle, a permanent and a temporary dwelling.

Proverbs 14:12.title: Proverbs 14:12
Proverbs 14:12.content: end thereof—or, "reward," what results (compare Pr 5:4). ways of death—leading to it.

Proverbs 14:13.title: Proverbs 14:13
Proverbs 14:13.content: The preceding sentiment illustrated by the disappointments of a wicked or untimely joy.

Proverbs 14:14.title: Proverbs 14:14
Proverbs 14:14.content: filled … ways—receive retribution (Pr 1:31). a good man … himself—literally, "is away from such," will not associate with him.

Proverbs 14:15.title: Proverbs 14:15
Proverbs 14:15.content: The simple … word—He is credulous, not from love, but heedlessness (Pr 13:16).

Proverbs 14:17.title: Proverbs 14:17
Proverbs 14:17.content: He … angry—literally, "short of anger" (compare Pr 14:29, opposite idea). man … hated—that is, the deliberate evildoer is more hated than the rash.

Proverbs 14:18.title: Proverbs 14:18
Proverbs 14:18.content: inherit—as a portion (compare Pr 3:35). are crowned—literally, "are surrounded with it," abound in it.

Proverbs 14:19.title: Proverbs 14:19
Proverbs 14:19.content: Describes the humbling of the wicked by the punishment their sins incur.

Proverbs 14:20.title: Proverbs 14:20
Proverbs 14:20.content: This sad but true picture of human nature is not given approvingly, but only as a fact.

Proverbs 14:21.title: Proverbs 14:21
Proverbs 14:21.content: For such contempt of the poor is contrasted as sinful with the virtuous compassion of the good.

Proverbs 14:22.title: Proverbs 14:22
Proverbs 14:22.content: As usual, the interrogative negative strengthens the affirmative. mercy and truth—that is, God's (Ps 57:3; 61:7).

Proverbs 14:23.title: Proverbs 14:23
Proverbs 14:23.content: labour—painful diligence. talk … penury—idle and vain promises and plans.

Proverbs 14:24.title: Proverbs 14:24
Proverbs 14:24.content: (Compare Pr 3:16). foolishness … folly—Folly remains, or produces folly; it has no benefit.

Proverbs 14:25.title: Proverbs 14:25
Proverbs 14:25.content: Life often depends on truth-telling. a deceitful … lies—He that breathes out lies is deceit, not to be trusted (Pr 14:5).

Proverbs 14:26.title: Proverbs 14:26
Proverbs 14:26.content: The blessings of piety descend to children (Pr 13:22; 20:7; Ex 20:6).

Proverbs 14:27.title: Proverbs 14:27
Proverbs 14:27.content: (Compare Pr 13:14). fear of the Lord—or, "law of the wise," is wisdom (Ps 111:10).

Proverbs 14:28.title: Proverbs 14:28
Proverbs 14:28.content: The teaching of a true political economy.

Proverbs 14:29.title: Proverbs 14:29
Proverbs 14:29.content: slow … understanding—(Compare Pr 14:17). hasty—(Compare Pr 14:17). exalteth folly—makes it conspicuous, as if delighting to honor it.

Proverbs 14:30.title: Proverbs 14:30
Proverbs 14:30.content: A sound heart—both literally and figuratively, a source of health; in the latter sense, opposed to the known effect of evil passions on health.

Proverbs 14:31.title: Proverbs 14:31
Proverbs 14:31.content: reproacheth his Maker—who is the God of such, as well as of the rich (Pr 22:2; Job 31:15; and specially 1Sa 2:8; Ps 113:7).

Proverbs 14:32.title: Proverbs 14:32
Proverbs 14:32.content: driven—thrust out violently (compare Ps 35:5, 6). hath hope—trusteth (Pr 10:2; 11:4; Ps 2:12), implying assurance of help.

Proverbs 14:33.title: Proverbs 14:33
Proverbs 14:33.content: resteth—preserved in quietness for use, while fools blazon their folly (Pr 12:23; 13:16).

Proverbs 14:34.title: Proverbs 14:34
Proverbs 14:34.content: Righteousness—just principles and actions. exalteth—raises to honor. is a reproach—brings on them the ill-will of others (compare Pr 13:6).

Proverbs 14:35.title: Proverbs 14:35
Proverbs 14:35.content: wise—discreet or prudent. causeth shame—(Pr 10:5; 12:4) acts basely.

Proverbs 15:1.title: Proverbs 15:1
Proverbs 15:1.content: soft—tender or gentle. turneth … wrath—from any one. stir up—as a smouldering fire is excited.

Proverbs 15:2.title: Proverbs 15:2
Proverbs 15:2.content: useth … aright—commends knowledge by its proper use. poureth out—utters abundantly (Pr 12:23), and so disgusts others.

Proverbs 15:4.title: Proverbs 15:4
Proverbs 15:4.content: A wholesome tongue—(Compare Margin), pacifying and soothing language. tree of life—(Pr 3:18; 11:30). perverseness therein—cross, ill-natured language. breach … spirit—(compare Isa 65:14, Hebrew), grieves, instead of appeasing.

Proverbs 15:7.title: Proverbs 15:7
Proverbs 15:7.content: (Compare Pr 10:20, 21). heart … not so—not right, or vain.

Proverbs 15:8.title: Proverbs 15:8-9
Proverbs 15:8.content: The sacrifice [and] prayer—are acts of worship. way … followeth … righteousness—denote conduct. God's regard for the worship and deeds of the righteous and wicked respectively, so stated in Ps 50:17; Isa 1:11.

Proverbs 15:9.title: Proverbs 15:8-9
Proverbs 15:9.content: The sacrifice [and] prayer—are acts of worship. way … followeth … righteousness—denote conduct. God's regard for the worship and deeds of the righteous and wicked respectively, so stated in Ps 50:17; Isa 1:11.

Proverbs 15:10.title: Proverbs 15:10
Proverbs 15:10.content: (Compare Pr 10:17). the way—that in which God would have him to go (Pr 2:13; Ps 119:1).

Proverbs 15:11.title: Proverbs 15:11
Proverbs 15:11.content: Hell—(Ps 16:10). destruction—or, "Abaddon," the place of the destroyer. All the unseen world is open to God, much more men's hearts.

Proverbs 15:12.title: Proverbs 15:12
Proverbs 15:12.content: (Compare Pr 9:8). go unto the wise—to be instructed.

Proverbs 15:13.title: Proverbs 15:13
Proverbs 15:13.content: maketh … countenance—or, "benefits the countenance." spirit is broken—and so the countenance is sad.

Proverbs 15:14.title: Proverbs 15:14
Proverbs 15:14.content: (Compare Pr 10:21, 22). The wise grow wiser, the fools more foolish (Pr 9:9).

Proverbs 15:15.title: Proverbs 15:15
Proverbs 15:15.content: The state of the heart governs the outward condition. evil—sad, contrasted with the cheerfulness of a feast.

Proverbs 15:16.title: Proverbs 15:16
Proverbs 15:16.content: trouble—agitation, implying the anxieties and perplexities attending wealth held by worldlings (Pr 16:18; 1Ti 6:6).

Proverbs 15:17.title: Proverbs 15:17
Proverbs 15:17.content: dinner—or, "allowance" (2Ki 25:30)— of herbs—and that the plainest. and hatred—(compare Pr 10:12, 18).

Proverbs 15:19.title: Proverbs 15:19
Proverbs 15:19.content: The difficulties of the slothful result from want of energy; the righteous find a plain [and open] way—literally, "a highway," by diligence (1Sa 10:7; Ps 1:3).

Proverbs 15:21.title: Proverbs 15:21
Proverbs 15:21.content: walketh uprightly—and so finds his joy (Pr 3:6; 10:23).

Proverbs 15:22.title: Proverbs 15:22
Proverbs 15:22.content: Without counsel—or, "deliberation," implying a wise deference to the opinions of the wise and good, contrasted with rashness.

Proverbs 15:23.title: Proverbs 15:23
Proverbs 15:23.content: Good advice blesses the giver and receiver.

Proverbs 15:24.title: Proverbs 15:24
Proverbs 15:24.content: (Compare Col 3:2). Holy purposes prevent sinning, and so its evils.

Proverbs 15:25.title: Proverbs 15:25
Proverbs 15:25.content: The most desolate who have God's aid have more permanent good than the self-reliant sinner (Pr 2:22; 12:7). border—or, "boundary for possessions" (Ps 78:54).

Proverbs 15:26.title: Proverbs 15:26
Proverbs 15:26.content: are pleasant words—that is, pleasing to God (Pr 8:8, 9).

Proverbs 15:27.title: Proverbs 15:27
Proverbs 15:27.content: (Compare Pr 11:17). Avarice brings trouble to him and his. hateth gifts—or, "bribes" (Ex 23:8; Ps 15:5), and is not avaricious.

Proverbs 15:28.title: Proverbs 15:28
Proverbs 15:28.content: (Compare Pr 15:14; 10:11). Caution is the fruit of wisdom; rashness of folly.

Proverbs 15:29.title: Proverbs 15:29
Proverbs 15:29.content: far … wicked—in His love and favor (Ps 22:11; 119:155).

Proverbs 15:30.title: Proverbs 15:30
Proverbs 15:30.content: light of the eyes—(Pr 13:9). What gives light rejoiceth the heart, by relieving from anxiety as to our course; so good report—or, "doctrine" (Isa 28:9; 53:1), maketh … fat—or, "gives prosperity" (Pr 3:13-17; 9:11). The last clause is illustrated by the first.

Proverbs 15:31.title: Proverbs 15:31-32
Proverbs 15:31.content: (Compare Pr 10:17). reproof of life—which leads to life. abideth … wise—is numbered among them.

Proverbs 15:32.title: Proverbs 15:31-32
Proverbs 15:32.content: (Compare Pr 10:17). reproof of life—which leads to life. abideth … wise—is numbered among them.

Proverbs 15:32.title: Proverbs 15:32
Proverbs 15:32.content: refuseth—or, "neglects," "passes by" (Pr 1:25; 4:15). despiseth … soul—so acts as if esteeming its interests of no value.

Proverbs 15:33.title: Proverbs 15:33
Proverbs 15:33.content: The fear … wisdom—Wisdom instructs in true piety. before … humility—(compare Lu 24:26; 1Pe 1:11); opposite (compare Pr 16:18).

Proverbs 16:1.title: Proverbs 16:1
Proverbs 16:1.content: preparations—schemes. in man—or literally, "to man," belonging, or pertaining to him. the answer … Lord—The efficient ordering is from God: "Man proposes; God disposes."

Proverbs 16:2.title: Proverbs 16:2
Proverbs 16:2.content: clean—or, "faultless." weigheth—or, "tries," "judges," implying that they are faulty (Pr 21:2; 24:12).

Proverbs 16:3.title: Proverbs 16:3
Proverbs 16:3.content: (Compare Margin). Rely on God for success to your lawful purposes.

Proverbs 16:4.title: Proverbs 16:4
Proverbs 16:4.content: for himself—"for its answer," or "purpose," that is, according to God's plan; the wicked are for the day of evil (Ps 49:5; Jer 17:18); sinning and suffering answer to each other, are indissolubly united.

Proverbs 16:6.title: Proverbs 16:6
Proverbs 16:6.content: By mercy and truth—that is, God's (Ps 85:10); He effects the atonement, or covering of sin; and the principles of true piety incline men to depart from evil; or, "mercy" and "truth" may be man's, indicative of the gracious tempers which work instrumentally in procuring pardon. purged—expiated (as in Le 16:33; Isa 27:9, Hebrew).

Proverbs 16:10.title: Proverbs 16:10
Proverbs 16:10.content: The last clause depends on the first, expressing the importance of equity in decisions, so authoritative.

Proverbs 16:11.title: Proverbs 16:11
Proverbs 16:11.content: are the Lord's … his work—that is, what He has ordered, and hence should be observed by men.

Proverbs 16:12.title: Proverbs 16:12
Proverbs 16:12.content: Rulers are rightly expected, by their position, to hate evil; for their power is sustained by righteousness.

Proverbs 16:13.title: Proverbs 16:13
Proverbs 16:13.content: A specification of the general sentiment of Pr 16:12.

Proverbs 16:14.title: Proverbs 16:14
Proverbs 16:14.content: This wrath, so terrible and certain, like messengers of death (1Ki 2:25), can be appeased by the wise.

Proverbs 16:15.title: Proverbs 16:15
Proverbs 16:15.content: light of … countenance—favor (Ps 4:6). life—preserves it, or gives blessings which make it valuable. the latter rain—fell just before harvest and matured the crop; hence specially valuable (De 11:14).

Proverbs 16:17.title: Proverbs 16:17
Proverbs 16:17.content: The highway—A common, plain road represents the habitual course of the righteous in departing from evil. keepeth—observes.

Proverbs 16:18.title: Proverbs 16:18-19
Proverbs 16:18.content: (Compare Pr 15:33). Haughtiness and pride imply self-confidence which produces carelessness, and hence a fall—literally, "sliding."

Proverbs 16:19.title: Proverbs 16:18-19
Proverbs 16:19.content: (Compare Pr 15:33). Haughtiness and pride imply self-confidence which produces carelessness, and hence a fall—literally, "sliding."

Proverbs 16:19.title: Proverbs 16:19
Proverbs 16:19.content: divide the spoil—that is, conquer. Avoid the society of the proud (Jas 4:6).

Proverbs 16:20.title: Proverbs 16:20
Proverbs 16:20.content: handleth a matter—wisely considers "the word," that is, of God (compare Pr 13:13). trusteth—(Compare Ps 2:12; 118:8, 9).

Proverbs 16:21.title: Proverbs 16:21
Proverbs 16:21.content: wise in heart—who rightly consider duty. sweetness of the lips—eloquent discourse, persuades and instructs others.

Proverbs 16:22.title: Proverbs 16:22
Proverbs 16:22.content: Understanding—or, "discretion," is a constant source of blessing (Pr 13:14), benefiting others; but fools' best efforts are folly.

Proverbs 16:23.title: Proverbs 16:23
Proverbs 16:23.content: The heart is the source of wisdom flowing from the mouth.

Proverbs 16:24.title: Proverbs 16:24
Proverbs 16:24.content: (Compare Pr 15:26). Gentle, kind words, by soothing the mind, give the body health.

Proverbs 16:26.title: Proverbs 16:26
Proverbs 16:26.content: Diligence is a duty due to one's self, for his wants require labor.

Proverbs 16:27.title: Proverbs 16:27
Proverbs 16:27.content: ungodly man—(Compare Pr 6:12). diggeth up evil—labors for it. in his lips … fire—His words are calumniating (Jas 3:6).

Proverbs 16:30.title: Proverbs 16:30
Proverbs 16:30.content: He shutteth his eyes—denoting deep thought (Ps 64:6). moving his lips—or, "biting his lips"—a determined purpose (Pr 6:13).

Proverbs 16:31.title: Proverbs 16:31
Proverbs 16:31.content: (Compare Pr 20:29). if—or, which may be supplied properly, or without it the sense is as in Pr 3:16; 4:10, that piety is blessed with long life.

Proverbs 16:32.title: Proverbs 16:32
Proverbs 16:32.content: (Compare Pr 14:29). taketh a city—that is, by fighting.

Proverbs 16:33.title: Proverbs 16:33
Proverbs 16:33.content: Seemingly the most fortuitous events are ordered by God.

Proverbs 17:1.title: Proverbs 17:1
Proverbs 17:1.content: sacrifices—or, "feasts" made with part of them (compare Pr 7:14; Le 2:3; 7:31). with—literally, "of." strife—its product, or attendant.

Proverbs 17:2.title: Proverbs 17:2
Proverbs 17:2.content: (Compare Pr 14:35). causeth shame—(Pr 10:5). shall … inheritance—that is, share a brother's part (compare Nu 27:4, 7).

Proverbs 17:3.title: Proverbs 17:3
Proverbs 17:3.content: God only knows, as He tries (Ps 12:6; 66:10) the heart.

Proverbs 17:4.title: Proverbs 17:4
Proverbs 17:4.content: Wicked doers and speakers alike delight in calumny.

Proverbs 17:5.title: Proverbs 17:5
Proverbs 17:5.content: (Compare Pr 14:31). glad at calamities—rejoicing in others' evil. Such are rightly punished by God, who knows their hearts.

Proverbs 17:6.title: Proverbs 17:6
Proverbs 17:6.content: Prolonged posterity is a blessing, its cutting off a curse (Pr 13:22; Ps 109:13-15), hence children may glory in virtuous ancestry.

Proverbs 17:7.title: Proverbs 17:7
Proverbs 17:7.content: Excellent speech—(Compare Margin). Such language as ill suits a fool, as lying (ought to suit) a prince (Pr 16:12, 13).

Proverbs 17:8.title: Proverbs 17:8
Proverbs 17:8.content: One so corrupt as to take a bribe evinces his high estimate of it by subjection to its influence (Pr 18:16; 19:6).

Proverbs 17:9.title: Proverbs 17:9
Proverbs 17:9.content: seeketh love—(Compare Margin). The contrast is between the peace-maker and tale-bearer.

Proverbs 17:10.title: Proverbs 17:10
Proverbs 17:10.content: Reproof more affects the wise than severe scourging, fools.

Proverbs 17:11.title: Proverbs 17:11
Proverbs 17:11.content: Such meet just retribution (1Ki 2:25). a cruel messenger—one to inflict it.

Proverbs 17:12.title: Proverbs 17:12
Proverbs 17:12.content: They are less rational in anger than wild beasts.

Proverbs 17:14.title: Proverbs 17:14
Proverbs 17:14.content: letteth … water—as a breach in a dam. before … meddled with—before strife has become sharp, or, by an explanation better suiting the figure, before it rolls on, or increases.

Proverbs 17:15.title: Proverbs 17:15
Proverbs 17:15.content: abomination … Lord—as reversing His method of acting (Pr 3:32; 12:2).

Proverbs 17:16.title: Proverbs 17:16
Proverbs 17:16.content: Though wealth cannot buy wisdom for those who do not love it, yet wisdom procures wealth (Pr 3:16; 14:24).

Proverbs 17:17.title: Proverbs 17:17
Proverbs 17:17.content: To the second of these parallel clauses, there is an accession of meaning, that is, that a brother's love is specially seen in adversity.

Proverbs 17:18.title: Proverbs 17:18
Proverbs 17:18.content: (Compare Pr 6:1-5; 11:15). in the presence, &c.—that is, he either fails to consult his friend, or to follow his advice.

Proverbs 17:19.title: Proverbs 17:19
Proverbs 17:19.content: strife—contention is, and leads to, sin. he that exalteth his gate—gratifies a vain love of costly building. seeketh—or, "findeth," as if he sought (compare "loveth death," Pr 8:36).

Proverbs 17:20.title: Proverbs 17:20
Proverbs 17:20.content: The second clause advances on the first. The ill-natured fail of good, and the cavilling and fault-finding incur evil.

Proverbs 17:21.title: Proverbs 17:21
Proverbs 17:21.content: (Compare Pr 23:24). Different words are rendered by "fool," both denoting stupidity and impiety.

Proverbs 17:22.title: Proverbs 17:22
Proverbs 17:22.content: (Compare Pr 14:30; 15:13). The effect of the mind on the body is well known. medicine—or, "body," which better corresponds with "bone." drieth—as if the marrow were exhausted.

Proverbs 17:23.title: Proverbs 17:23
Proverbs 17:23.content: a gift … bosom—Money and other valuables were borne in a fold of the garment, called the bosom. to pervert—that is, by bribery.

Proverbs 17:24.title: Proverbs 17:24
Proverbs 17:24.content: Wisdom … him—ever an object of regard, while a fool's affections are unsettled.

Proverbs 17:26.title: Proverbs 17:26
Proverbs 17:26.content: Also—that is, Equally to be avoided are other sins: punishing good subjects, or resisting good rulers.

Proverbs 17:27.title: Proverbs 17:27-28
Proverbs 17:27.content: Prudence of speech is commended as is an excellent or calm spirit, not excited to vain conversation.

Proverbs 17:28.title: Proverbs 17:27-28
Proverbs 17:28.content: Prudence of speech is commended as is an excellent or calm spirit, not excited to vain conversation.

Proverbs 18:1.title: Proverbs 18:1
Proverbs 18:1.content: Through desire … seeketh—that is, seeks selfish gratification. intermeddleth … wisdom—or, "rushes on" (Pr 17:14) against all wisdom, or what is valuable (Pr 2:7).

Proverbs 18:2.title: Proverbs 18:2
Proverbs 18:2.content: that his heart … itself—that is, takes pleasure in revealing his folly (Pr 12:23; 15:2).

Proverbs 18:3.title: Proverbs 18:3
Proverbs 18:3.content: So surely are sin and punishment connected (Pr 16:4). wicked, for "wickedness," answers to ignominy, or the state of such; and contempt, the feeling of others to them; and to reproach, a manifestation of contempt.

Proverbs 18:4.title: Proverbs 18:4
Proverbs 18:4.content: Wise speech is like an exhaustless stream of benefit.

Proverbs 18:5.title: Proverbs 18:5
Proverbs 18:5.content: accept the person—(Compare Ps 82:2). "It is not good" is to be supplied before "to overthrow."

Proverbs 18:6.title: Proverbs 18:6-7
Proverbs 18:6.content: The quarrelsome bring trouble on themselves. Their rash language ensnares them (Pr 6:2).

Proverbs 18:7.title: Proverbs 18:6-7
Proverbs 18:7.content: The quarrelsome bring trouble on themselves. Their rash language ensnares them (Pr 6:2).

Proverbs 18:8.title: Proverbs 18:8
Proverbs 18:8.content: (Compare Pr 16:28). as wounds—not sustained by the Hebrew; better, as "sweet morsels," which men gladly swallow. innermost … belly—the mind, or heart (compare Pr 20:27-30; Ps 22:14).

Proverbs 18:9.title: Proverbs 18:9
Proverbs 18:9.content: One by failing to get, the other by wasting wealth, grows poor. waster—literally, "master of washing," a prodigal.

Proverbs 18:10.title: Proverbs 18:10
Proverbs 18:10.content: name of the Lord—manifested perfections (Ps 8:1; 20:2), as faithfulness, power, mercy, &c., on which men rely. is safe—literally, "set on high, out of danger" (Ps 18:2; 91:4).

Proverbs 18:11.title: Proverbs 18:11
Proverbs 18:11.content: contrasts with Pr 18:10 (compare Pr 10:15). Such is a vain trust (compare Ps 73:6).

Proverbs 18:13.title: Proverbs 18:13
Proverbs 18:13.content: Hasty speech evinces self-conceit, and ensures shame (Pr 26:12).

Proverbs 18:14.title: Proverbs 18:14
Proverbs 18:14.content: infirmity—bodily sickness, or outward evil. The spirit, which sustains, being wounded, no support is left, except, as implied, in God.

Proverbs 18:16.title: Proverbs 18:16
Proverbs 18:16.content: (Compare Pr 17:8, 23). Disapproval of the fact stated is implied.

Proverbs 18:17.title: Proverbs 18:17
Proverbs 18:17.content: One-sided statements are not reliable. searcheth—thoroughly (Pr 17:9, 19).

Proverbs 18:18.title: Proverbs 18:18
Proverbs 18:18.content: The lot—whose disposal is of God (Pr 16:13), may, properly used, be a right mode of settling disputes.

Proverbs 18:19.title: Proverbs 18:19
Proverbs 18:19.content: No feuds so difficult of adjustment as those of relatives; hence great care should be used to avoid them.

Proverbs 18:20.title: Proverbs 18:20
Proverbs 18:20.content: (Compare Pr 12:14; 13:2). Men's words are the fruit, or, increase of his lips, and when good, benefit them. satisfied with—(Compare Pr 1:31; 14:14).

Proverbs 18:21.title: Proverbs 18:21
Proverbs 18:21.content: Death and life—or, the greatest evil and good. that love it—that is, the tongue, or its use for good or evil. eat … fruit—(Compare Pr 18:19; Jas 1:19).

Proverbs 18:22.title: Proverbs 18:22
Proverbs 18:22.content: The old versions supply "good" before the "wife," as the last clause and Pr 19:14 imply (compare Pr 31:10).

Proverbs 18:23.title: Proverbs 18:23
Proverbs 18:23.content: the rich … roughly—He is tolerated because rich, implying that the estimate of men by wealth is wrong.

Proverbs 18:24.title: Proverbs 18:24
Proverbs 18:24.content: A man … friendly—better, "A man … (is) to, or, may triumph (Ps 108:9), or, shout for joy (Ps 5:11), that is, may congratulate himself." Indeed, there is a Friend who is better than a brother; such is the "Friend of sinners" [Mt 11:19; Lu 7:34], who may have been before the writer's mind.

Proverbs 19:1.title: Proverbs 19:1
Proverbs 19:1.content: (Compare Pr 28:6). "Rich" for fool here. Integrity is better than riches (Pr 15:16, 17; 16:8).

Proverbs 19:2.title: Proverbs 19:2
Proverbs 19:2.content: The last illustrates the first clause. Rashness, the result of ignorance, brings trouble.

Proverbs 19:3.title: Proverbs 19:3
Proverbs 19:3.content: perverteth … way—turns him back from right (Pr 13:6; Jas 1:13); and he blames God for his failures.

Proverbs 19:4.title: Proverbs 19:4
Proverbs 19:4.content: (Compare Pr 14:20). Such facts are often adduced with implied disapprobation.

Proverbs 19:5.title: Proverbs 19:5
Proverbs 19:5.content: Compare Pr 19:9, where perish explains not escape here (compare Ps 88:9, 10).

Proverbs 19:8.title: Proverbs 19:8
Proverbs 19:8.content: (Compare Margin; Pr 15:32). loveth … soul—or, "himself," which he evinces by regarding his best interests. keepeth—or, "regards."

Proverbs 19:10.title: Proverbs 19:10
Proverbs 19:10.content: (Compare Pr 17:7). The fool is incapable of properly using pleasure as knowledge, yet for him to have it is less incongruous than the undue elevation of servants. Let each abide in his calling (1Co 7:20).

Proverbs 19:11.title: Proverbs 19:11
Proverbs 19:11.content: (Compare Pr 14:29; 16:32). This inculcation of a forgiving spirit shows that true religion is always the same (Mt 5:22-24).

Proverbs 19:12.title: Proverbs 19:12
Proverbs 19:12.content: (Compare Pr 16:14, 15; 20:2). A motive to submission to lawful authority.

Proverbs 19:13.title: Proverbs 19:13
Proverbs 19:13.content: calamity—literally, "calamities," varied and many. continual dropping—a perpetual annoyance, wearing out patience.

Proverbs 19:14.title: Proverbs 19:14
Proverbs 19:14.content: A contrast of men's gifts and God's, who, though author of both blessings, confers the latter by His more special providence. and—or, "but," implying that the evils of Pr 19:13 are only avoided by His care.

Proverbs 19:15.title: Proverbs 19:15
Proverbs 19:15.content: a deep sleep—a state of utter indifference. idle soul—or, "person" (compare Pr 10:4; 12:24).

Proverbs 19:16.title: Proverbs 19:16
Proverbs 19:16.content: (Compare Pr 10:17; 13:13). despiseth … ways—opposed to keeping or observing, neglects (Pr 16:17) (as unworthy of regard) his moral conduct.

Proverbs 19:17.title: Proverbs 19:17
Proverbs 19:17.content: (Compare Pr 14:21; Ps 37:26). hath pity—shown by acts (compare Margin).

Proverbs 19:18.title: Proverbs 19:18
Proverbs 19:18.content: (Compare Pr 13:24; 23:13). let not … spare—literally, "do not lift up thy soul" (Ps 24:4; 25:1), that is, do not desire to his death; a caution to passionate parents against angry chastisement.

Proverbs 19:19.title: Proverbs 19:19
Proverbs 19:19.content: Repeated efforts of kindness are lost on ill-natured persons.

Proverbs 19:20.title: Proverbs 19:20
Proverbs 19:20.content: (Compare Pr 13:18-20). latter end—(Pr 5:11). In youth prepare for age.

Proverbs 19:21.title: Proverbs 19:21
Proverbs 19:21.content: (Compare Pr 16:1, 9; Ps 33:10, 11). The failure of man's devices is implied.

Proverbs 19:22.title: Proverbs 19:22
Proverbs 19:22.content: desire—that is, to do good, indicates a kind disposition (Pr 11:23); and the poor thus affected are better than liars, who say and do not.

Proverbs 19:23.title: Proverbs 19:23
Proverbs 19:23.content: The fear … life—(Compare Pr 3:2). abide—or, "remain contented" (1Ti 4:8). not visited with evil—(Pr 10:3; Ps 37:25), as a judgment, in which sense visit is often used (Ps 89:32; Jer 6:15).

Proverbs 19:24.title: Proverbs 19:24
Proverbs 19:24.content: bosom—literally, a wide dish in which the hand was plunged in eating (Mt 26:23). Compare Pr 26:15, the sentiment expressed with equal irony and less exaggeration.

Proverbs 19:25.title: Proverbs 19:25
Proverbs 19:25.content: Such is the benefit of reproof; even the simple profit, much more the wise.

Proverbs 19:28.title: Proverbs 19:28
Proverbs 19:28.content: ungodly witness—(Compare Margin), one false by bad principles (compare Pr 6:12). scorneth judgment—sets at naught the dictates of justice. devoureth—literally, "swalloweth," as something delightful.

Proverbs 19:29.title: Proverbs 19:29
Proverbs 19:29.content: Their punishment is sure, fixed, and ready (compare Pr 3:34; 10:13).

Proverbs 20:1.title: Proverbs 20:1
Proverbs 20:1.content: mocker—scorner. Such men are made by wine. strong drink—made by spicing wine (compare Isa 5:11, 22); and it may include wine. raging—or boisterous as a drunkard. deceived—literally, "erring," or reeling.

Proverbs 20:2.title: Proverbs 20:2
Proverbs 20:2.content: (Compare Pr 19:12). Men who resist authority injure themselves (Ro 13:2).

Proverbs 20:3.title: Proverbs 20:3
Proverbs 20:3.content: to cease from strife—or, better, "to dwell from or without strife," denoting the habit of life. fool … meddling—(Pr 17:14).

Proverbs 20:5.title: Proverbs 20:5
Proverbs 20:5.content: Counsel … water—that is, deeply hidden (Pr 18:4; Ps 13:2). The wise can discern well.

Proverbs 20:7.title: Proverbs 20:7
Proverbs 20:7.content: The conduct of good men proclaims their sound principles. God's covenant and their good example secure blessing to their children (Pr 4:26; Ps 112:1, 2).

Proverbs 20:8.title: Proverbs 20:8
Proverbs 20:8.content: As in Pr 14:35; 16:10, 15, this is the character of a good king, not of all kings.

Proverbs 20:9.title: Proverbs 20:9
Proverbs 20:9.content: The interrogation in the affirmative strengthens the implied negation (compare Job 15:14; Ec 7:20).

Proverbs 20:10.title: Proverbs 20:10
Proverbs 20:10.content: Various measures, implying that some are wrong (compare Pr 11:1; 16:11).

Proverbs 20:11.title: Proverbs 20:11
Proverbs 20:11.content: The conduct of children even is the best test of principle (compare Mt 7:16).

Proverbs 20:12.title: Proverbs 20:12
Proverbs 20:12.content: Hence, of course, God will know all you do (Ps 94:9).

Proverbs 20:13.title: Proverbs 20:13
Proverbs 20:13.content: Activity and diligence contrasted with sloth (Pr 6:9; 10:11). lest … poverty—literally, "be deprived of inheritance."

Proverbs 20:14.title: Proverbs 20:14
Proverbs 20:14.content: when … his way—implying that he goes about boasting of his bargains.

Proverbs 20:15.title: Proverbs 20:15
Proverbs 20:15.content: The contrast denotes the greater value of knowledge (compare Pr 3:14-16).

Proverbs 20:16.title: Proverbs 20:16
Proverbs 20:16.content: Take his garment—implies severe exaction, justified by the surety's rashness. a strange woman—by some readings "strangers," but the former here, and in Pr 27:13, is allowable, and strengthens the sense. The debauchee is less reliable than the merely careless.

Proverbs 20:17.title: Proverbs 20:17
Proverbs 20:17.content: Bread … sweet—either as unlawfully (Pr 9:17) or easily obtained. mouth … gravel—well expresses the pain and grief given at last.

Proverbs 20:18.title: Proverbs 20:18
Proverbs 20:18.content: (Compare Pr 15:22). Be careful and considerate in important plans.

Proverbs 20:19.title: Proverbs 20:19
Proverbs 20:19.content: Those who love to tell news will hardly keep secrets. flattereth … lips—(compare Margin; Pr 1:10). meddle … him—literally, "join," or "associate with."

Proverbs 20:21.title: Proverbs 20:21
Proverbs 20:21.content: gotten hastily—contrary to God's providence (Pr 28:20), implying its unjust or easy attainment; hence the man is punished, or spends freely what he got easily (compare Pr 20:17).

Proverbs 20:24.title: Proverbs 20:24
Proverbs 20:24.content: Man's goings—literally, "Stately steppings of a strong man." a man—any common man. understand—or, "perceive."

Proverbs 20:25.title: Proverbs 20:25
Proverbs 20:25.content: devoureth … holy—or, better, "who rashly speaks promises," or "devotes what is holy," consecrating any thing. This suits better the last clause, which expresses a similar view of the results of rashly vowing.

Proverbs 20:26.title: Proverbs 20:26
Proverbs 20:26.content: (Compare Pr 20:8). bringeth … over them—The wheel was used for threshing grain. The figure denotes severity (compare Am 1:3).

Proverbs 20:27.title: Proverbs 20:27
Proverbs 20:27.content: The spirit … Lord—Men's minds are God's gifts, and thus able to search one another (compare Pr 20:5; Pr 18:8, 17; 1Co 2:11).

Proverbs 20:29.title: Proverbs 20:29
Proverbs 20:29.content: The glory of young men … the beauty of old men—Each age has its peculiar excellence (Pr 16:31).

Proverbs 20:30.title: Proverbs 20:30
Proverbs 20:30.content: blueness—literally, "joining," the process of uniting the edges of a wound throws off purulent matter. stripes … belly—So punishment provides healing of soul (Pr 18:8), by deterring from evil courses.

Proverbs 21:1.title: Proverbs 21:1
Proverbs 21:1.content: rivers—irrigating channels (Ps 1:3), whose course was easily turned (compare De 11:10). God disposes even kings as He pleases (Pr 16:9; Ps 33:15).

Proverbs 21:4.title: Proverbs 21:4
Proverbs 21:4.content: high look—(Compare Margin; Ps 131:1). proud heart—or, "heart of breadth," one that is swollen (compare Ps 101:5). ploughing—better "lamp," a frequent figure for prosperity (Pr 20:20); hence joy or delight.

Proverbs 21:5.title: Proverbs 21:5
Proverbs 21:5.content: The contrast is between steady industry and rashness (compare Pr 19:2).

Proverbs 21:6.title: Proverbs 21:6
Proverbs 21:6.content: The getting—or, "what is obtained" (compare Job 7:2; Jer 22:13, Hebrew). vanity … to and fro—as fleeting as chaff or stubble in the wind (compare Pr 20:17-21; Ps 62:10). Such gettings are unsatisfactory. them … death—act as if they did (Pr 8:36; 17:19).

Proverbs 21:7.title: Proverbs 21:7
Proverbs 21:7.content: robbery—or, "destruction," especially oppression, of which they are authors. shall destroy—literally, "cut with a saw" (1Ki 7:9), that is, utterly ruin them. Their sins shall be visited on them in kind. to do judgment—what is just and right.

Proverbs 21:8.title: Proverbs 21:8
Proverbs 21:8.content: of man—any one; his way is opposed to truth, and also estranged from it. The pure proves himself such by his right conduct.

Proverbs 21:9.title: Proverbs 21:9
Proverbs 21:9.content: corner—a turret or arbor on the roof. brawling—or contentious. wide house—literally, "house of fellowship," large enough for several families.

Proverbs 21:10.title: Proverbs 21:10
Proverbs 21:10.content: So strongly does he desire to do evil (Ps 10:3; Ec 8:11), that he will not even spare his friend if in his way.

Proverbs 21:11.title: Proverbs 21:11
Proverbs 21:11.content: (Compare Pr 19:25). That which the simple learn by the terrors of punishment, the wise learn by teaching.

Proverbs 21:12.title: Proverbs 21:12
Proverbs 21:12.content: (Compare Ps 37:35-38; 73:17, 20). house—family or interests. overthroweth—either supply "God" (compare Pr 10:24), or the word is used impersonally.

Proverbs 21:13.title: Proverbs 21:13
Proverbs 21:13.content: The principles of retribution, often taught (compare Ps 18:26; Mt 7:1-12).

Proverbs 21:14.title: Proverbs 21:14
Proverbs 21:14.content: The effect of bribery (Pr 17:23) is enhanced by secrecy, as the bribed person does not wish his motives made known.

Proverbs 21:15.title: Proverbs 21:15
Proverbs 21:15.content: But the just love right and need no bribes. The wicked at last meet destruction, though for a time happy in concealing corruption.

Proverbs 21:16.title: Proverbs 21:16
Proverbs 21:16.content: the way of understanding—(Compare Pr 12:26; 14:22). remain—that is, rest as at a journey's end; death will be his unchanging home.

Proverbs 21:18.title: Proverbs 21:18
Proverbs 21:18.content: (Compare Pr 11:8). By suffering what they had devised for the righteous, or brought on them, the wicked became their ransom, in the usual sense of substitutes (compare Jos 7:26; Es 7:9).

Proverbs 21:20.title: Proverbs 21:20
Proverbs 21:20.content: The wise, by diligence and care, lay up and increase wealth, while fools spend—literally, "swallow it up," greedily.

Proverbs 21:21.title: Proverbs 21:21
Proverbs 21:21.content: He who tries to act justly and kindly (Ps 34:14) will prosper and obtain justice and honor.

Proverbs 21:22.title: Proverbs 21:22
Proverbs 21:22.content: "Wisdom is better than strength" (Ec 7:19; 9:15). strength … thereof—that in which they confide.

Proverbs 21:24.title: Proverbs 21:24
Proverbs 21:24.content: The reproachful name is deserved by those who treat others with anger and contempt.

Proverbs 21:25.title: Proverbs 21:25
Proverbs 21:25.content: desire—that is, of ease and idleness brings him to starvation.

Proverbs 21:26.title: Proverbs 21:26
