Proverbs 25:23.content: Better, "As the north wind bringeth forth (Ps 90:2) or produces rain, so does a concealed or slandering tongue produce anger."

Proverbs 25:25.title: Proverbs 25:25
Proverbs 25:25.content: (Compare Pr 25:13). good news—that is, of some loved interest or absent friend, the more grateful as coming from afar.

Proverbs 25:26.title: Proverbs 25:26
Proverbs 25:26.content: From troubled fountains and corrupt springs no healthy water is to be had, so when the righteous are oppressed by the wicked, their power for good is lessened or destroyed.

Proverbs 25:27.title: Proverbs 25:27
Proverbs 25:27.content: Satiety surfeits (Pr 25:16); so men who are self-glorious find shame. is not glory—"not" is supplied from the first clause, or "is grievous," in which sense a similar word is used (Pr 27:2).

Proverbs 25:28.title: Proverbs 25:28
Proverbs 25:28.content: Such are exposed to the incursions of evil thoughts and successful temptations.

Proverbs 26:1.title: Proverbs 26:1
Proverbs 26:1.content: The incongruities of nature illustrate also those of the moral world. The fool's unworthiness is also implied (Pr 17:7; 19:10).

Proverbs 26:2.title: Proverbs 26:2
Proverbs 26:2.content: Though not obvious to us, the bird—literally, "sparrow"—and swallow—have an object in their motions, so penal evil falls on none without a reason.

Proverbs 26:3.title: Proverbs 26:3
Proverbs 26:3.content: The rod is as much needed by fools and as well suited to them, as whips and bridles are for beasts.

Proverbs 26:4.title: Proverbs 26:4-5
Proverbs 26:4.content: Answer not—that is, approvingly by like folly.

Proverbs 26:5.title: Proverbs 26:4-5
Proverbs 26:5.content: Answer not—that is, approvingly by like folly.

Proverbs 26:6.title: Proverbs 26:6
Proverbs 26:6.content: A fool fails by folly as surely as if he were maimed. drinketh damage—that is, gets it abundantly (Job 15:16; 34:7).

Proverbs 26:7.title: Proverbs 26:7
Proverbs 26:7.content: legs … equal—or, "take away the legs," or "the legs … are weak." In any case the idea is that they are the occasion of an awkwardness, such as the fool shows in using a parable or proverb (see Introduction; Pr 17:7).

Proverbs 26:8.title: Proverbs 26:8
Proverbs 26:8.content: A stone, bound in a sling, is useless; so honor, conferred on a fool, is thrown away.

Proverbs 26:9.title: Proverbs 26:9
Proverbs 26:9.content: As vexatious and unmanageable as a thorn in a drunkard's hand is a parable to a fool. He will be as apt to misuse is as to use it rightly.

Proverbs 26:10.title: Proverbs 26:10
Proverbs 26:10.content: Various versions of this are proposed (compare Margin). Better perhaps—"Much He injures (or literally, "wounds") all who reward," &c., that is, society is injured by encouraging evil men. transgressors—may be rendered "vagrants." The word "God" is improperly supplied.

Proverbs 26:11.title: Proverbs 26:11
Proverbs 26:11.content: returneth … folly—Though disgusting to others, the fool delights in his folly.

Proverbs 26:12.title: Proverbs 26:12
Proverbs 26:12.content: The self-conceited are taught with more difficulty than the stupid.

Proverbs 26:16.title: Proverbs 26:16
Proverbs 26:16.content: The thoughtless being ignorant of their ignorance are conceited.

Proverbs 26:17.title: Proverbs 26:17
Proverbs 26:17.content: meddleth—as in Pr 20:19; 24:21; as either holding a dog by the ears or letting him go involves danger, so success in another man's strife or failure involves a useless risk of reputation, does no good, and may do us harm.

Proverbs 26:20.title: Proverbs 26:20-21
Proverbs 26:20.content: The talebearers foster (Pr 16:28), and the contentious excite, strife.

Proverbs 26:21.title: Proverbs 26:20-21
Proverbs 26:21.content: The talebearers foster (Pr 16:28), and the contentious excite, strife.

Proverbs 26:23.title: Proverbs 26:23
Proverbs 26:23.content: Warm professions can no more give value to insincerity than silver coating to rude earthenware.

Proverbs 26:24.title: Proverbs 26:24
Proverbs 26:24.content: dissembleth—though an unusual sense of the word (compare Margin), is allowable, and better suits the context, which sets forth hypocrisy.

Proverbs 26:25.title: Proverbs 26:25
Proverbs 26:25.content: Sentiment of Pr 26:24 carried out. seven abominations in his heart—that is, very many (compare Pr 24:16).

Proverbs 26:26.title: Proverbs 26:26-27
Proverbs 26:26.content: Deceit will at last be exposed, and the wicked by their own arts often bring on retribution (compare Pr 12:13; Ps 7:16; 9:17, &c.).

Proverbs 26:27.title: Proverbs 26:26-27
Proverbs 26:27.content: Deceit will at last be exposed, and the wicked by their own arts often bring on retribution (compare Pr 12:13; Ps 7:16; 9:17, &c.).

Proverbs 26:28.title: Proverbs 26:28
Proverbs 26:28.content: Men hate those they injure. A lying tongue—"lips" for the persons (compare Pr 4:24; Ps 12:3).

Proverbs 27:1.title: Proverbs 27:1
Proverbs 27:1.content: Do not confide implicitly in your plans (Pr 16:9; 19:21; Jas 4:13-15).

Proverbs 27:3.title: Proverbs 27:3
Proverbs 27:3.content: heavy—The literal sense of "heavy," applied to material subjects, illustrates its figurative, "grievous," applied to moral. a fool's wrath—is unreasonable and excessive.

Proverbs 27:4.title: Proverbs 27:4
Proverbs 27:4.content: envy—or, "jealousy" (compare Margin; Pr 6:34), is more unappeasable than the simpler bad passions.

Proverbs 27:5.title: Proverbs 27:5-6
Proverbs 27:5.content: secret love—not manifested in acts is useless; and even, if its exhibition by rebukes wounds us, such love is preferable to the frequent (compare Margin), and hence deceitful, kisses of an enemy.

Proverbs 27:6.title: Proverbs 27:5-6
Proverbs 27:6.content: secret love—not manifested in acts is useless; and even, if its exhibition by rebukes wounds us, such love is preferable to the frequent (compare Margin), and hence deceitful, kisses of an enemy.

Proverbs 27:7.title: Proverbs 27:7
Proverbs 27:7.content: The luxury of wealth confers less happiness than the healthy appetite of labor.

Proverbs 27:8.title: Proverbs 27:8
Proverbs 27:8.content: Such are not only out of place, but out of duty and in danger.

Proverbs 27:9.title: Proverbs 27:9
Proverbs 27:9.content: rejoice the heart—the organ of perceiving what pleases the senses. sweetness … counsel—or, "wise counsel is also pleasing."

Proverbs 27:10.title: Proverbs 27:10
Proverbs 27:10.content: Adhere to tried friends. The ties of blood may be less reliable than those of genuine friendship.

Proverbs 27:11.title: Proverbs 27:11
Proverbs 27:11.content: The wisdom of children both reflects credit on parents and contributes to their aid in difficulties.

Proverbs 27:14.title: Proverbs 27:14
Proverbs 27:14.content: Excessive zeal in praising raises suspicions of selfishness.

Proverbs 27:15.title: Proverbs 27:15
Proverbs 27:15.content: (Compare Pr 19:13). very … day—literally, "a day of showers."

Proverbs 27:16.title: Proverbs 27:16
Proverbs 27:16.content: hideth—or, "restrains" (that is, tries to do it); is as fruitless an effort, as that of holding the wind. the ointment of his right hand—the organ of power (Ps 17:7; 18:35). His right hand endeavors to repress perfume, but vainly. Some prefer: "His right hand comes on oil," that is, "cannot take hold." Such a woman cannot be tamed.

Proverbs 27:17.title: Proverbs 27:17
Proverbs 27:17.content: a man sharpeneth … friend—that is, conversation promotes intelligence, which the face exhibits.

Proverbs 27:18.title: Proverbs 27:18
Proverbs 27:18.content: Diligence secures a reward, even for the humble servant.

Proverbs 27:19.title: Proverbs 27:19
Proverbs 27:19.content: We may see our characters in the developed tempers of others.

Proverbs 27:20.title: Proverbs 27:20
Proverbs 27:20.content: Men's cupidity is as insatiable as the grave.

Proverbs 27:21.title: Proverbs 27:21
Proverbs 27:21.content: Praise tests character. a man to his praise—according to his praise, as he bears it. Thus vain men seek it, weak men are inflated by it, wise men disregard it, &c.

Proverbs 27:22.title: Proverbs 27:22
Proverbs 27:22.content: The obstinate wickedness of such is incurable by the heaviest inflictions.

Proverbs 27:23.title: Proverbs 27:23-24
Proverbs 27:23.content: flocks—constituted the staple of wealth. It is only by care and diligence that the most solid possessions can be perpetuated (Pr 23:5).

Proverbs 27:24.title: Proverbs 27:23-24
Proverbs 27:24.content: flocks—constituted the staple of wealth. It is only by care and diligence that the most solid possessions can be perpetuated (Pr 23:5).

Proverbs 27:25.title: Proverbs 27:25-27
Proverbs 27:25.content: The fact that providential arrangements furnish the means of competence to those who properly use them is another motive to diligence (compare Ps 65:9-13). The hay appeareth—literally, "Grass appeareth" (Job 40:15; Ps 104:14).

Proverbs 27:26.title: Proverbs 27:25-27
Proverbs 27:26.content: The fact that providential arrangements furnish the means of competence to those who properly use them is another motive to diligence (compare Ps 65:9-13). The hay appeareth—literally, "Grass appeareth" (Job 40:15; Ps 104:14).

Proverbs 27:27.title: Proverbs 27:25-27
Proverbs 27:27.content: The fact that providential arrangements furnish the means of competence to those who properly use them is another motive to diligence (compare Ps 65:9-13). The hay appeareth—literally, "Grass appeareth" (Job 40:15; Ps 104:14).

Proverbs 28:1.title: Proverbs 28:1
Proverbs 28:1.content: A bad conscience makes men timid; the righteous are alone truly bold (Pr 14:26; Ps 27:1).

Proverbs 28:2.title: Proverbs 28:2
Proverbs 28:2.content: Anarchy producing contending rulers shortens the reign of each. but by a man … prolonged—or, "by a man of understanding—that is, a good ruler—he who knows or regards the right, that is, a good citizen, shall prolong (his days)." Good rulers are a blessing to the people. Bad government as a punishment for evil is contrasted with good as blessing to the good.

Proverbs 28:3.title: Proverbs 28:3
Proverbs 28:3.content: A poor man, &c.—Such, in power, exact more severely, and so leave subjects bare.

Proverbs 28:4.title: Proverbs 28:4
Proverbs 28:4.content: They that forsake … wicked—Wrongdoers encourage one another.

Proverbs 28:5.title: Proverbs 28:5
Proverbs 28:5.content: (Compare Joh 7:17). Ignorance of moral truth is due to unwillingness to know it.

Proverbs 28:6.title: Proverbs 28:6
Proverbs 28:6.content: (Compare Pr 10:6). Riches cannot compensate for sin, nor the want of them affect integrity.

Proverbs 28:8.title: Proverbs 28:8
Proverbs 28:8.content: usury … unjust gain—(Compare Margin). The two terms, meaning nearly the same, may denote excessive interest. God's providence directs the proper use of wealth.

Proverbs 28:9.title: Proverbs 28:9
Proverbs 28:9.content: (Compare Pr 15:8; 21:27). hearing—that is, obeying. God requires sincere worshippers (Ps 66:18; Joh 4:24).

Proverbs 28:11.title: Proverbs 28:11
Proverbs 28:11.content: A poor but wise man can discover (and expose) the rich and self-conceited.

Proverbs 28:12.title: Proverbs 28:12
Proverbs 28:12.content: great glory—or, cause for it to a people, for the righteous rejoice in good, and righteousness exalts a nation (Pr 14:34). a man … hidden—that is, the good retire, or all kinds try to escape a wicked rule.

Proverbs 28:13.title: Proverbs 28:13
Proverbs 28:13.content: (Compare Ps 32:3-5). Concealment of sin delivers none from God's wrath, but He shows mercy to the humble penitent (Ps 51:4).

Proverbs 28:14.title: Proverbs 28:14
Proverbs 28:14.content: feareth—that is, God, and so repents. hardeneth his heart—makes himself insensible to sin, and so will not repent (Pr 14:16; 29:1).

Proverbs 28:15.title: Proverbs 28:15
Proverbs 28:15.content: The rapacity and cruelty of such beasts well represent some wicked men (compare Ps 7:2; 17:12).

Proverbs 28:16.title: Proverbs 28:16
Proverbs 28:16.content: The prince … understanding—that is, He does not perceive that oppression jeopards his success. Covetousness often produces oppression, hence the contrast.

Proverbs 28:17.title: Proverbs 28:17
Proverbs 28:17.content: doeth violence … blood, &c.—or, that is oppressed by the blood of life (Ge 9:6), which he has taken. to the pit—the grave or destruction (Pr 1:12; Job 33:18-24; Ps 143:7). stay him—sustain or deliver him.

Proverbs 28:18.title: Proverbs 28:18
Proverbs 28:18.content: (Compare Pr 10:9; 17:20). Double dealing is eventually fatal.

Proverbs 28:19.title: Proverbs 28:19
Proverbs 28:19.content: (Compare Pr 10:4; 20:4). vain persons—idle, useless drones, implying that they are also wicked (Pr 12:11; Ps 26:4).

Proverbs 28:20.title: Proverbs 28:20
Proverbs 28:20.content: maketh haste … rich—implying deceit or fraud (Pr 20:21), and so opposed to "faithful" or reliable.

Proverbs 28:21.title: Proverbs 28:21
Proverbs 28:21.content: respect of persons—(Pr 24:23). Such are led to evil by the slightest motive.

Proverbs 28:22.title: Proverbs 28:22
Proverbs 28:22.content: (Compare Pr 28:20). evil eye—in the general sense of Pr 23:6, here more specific for covetousness (compare Pr 22:9; Mt 20:15). poverty … him—by God's providence.

Proverbs 28:23.title: Proverbs 28:23
Proverbs 28:23.content: (Compare Pr 9:8, 9; 27:5). Those benefited by reproof will love their monitors.

Proverbs 28:24.title: Proverbs 28:24
Proverbs 28:24.content: (Compare Mt 15:4-6). Such, though heirs, are virtually thieves, to be ranked with highwaymen.

Proverbs 28:25.title: Proverbs 28:25
Proverbs 28:25.content: of a proud heart—literally, "puffed up of soul"—that is, self-confident, and hence overbearing and litigious. made fat—or, "prosperous" (Pr 11:25; 16:20).

Proverbs 28:26.title: Proverbs 28:26
Proverbs 28:26.content: (Compare Pr 3:6-8). walketh wisely—that is, trusting in God (Pr 22:17-19).

Proverbs 28:27.title: Proverbs 28:27
Proverbs 28:27.content: (Compare Pr 11:24-26). hideth his eyes—as the face (Ps 27:9; 69:17), denotes inattention.

Proverbs 28:28.title: Proverbs 28:28
Proverbs 28:28.content: The elevation of the wicked to power drives men to seek refuge from tyranny (compare Pr 28:12; 11:10; Ps 12:8).

Proverbs 29:1.title: Proverbs 29:1
Proverbs 29:1.content: hardeneth … neck—obstinately refuses counsel (2Ki 17:14; Ne 9:16). destroyed—literally, "shivered" or "utterly broken to pieces." without remedy—literally, "without healing" or repairing.

Proverbs 29:2.title: Proverbs 29:2
Proverbs 29:2.content: (Compare Pr 11:10; 28:28). in authority—(Compare Margin), increased in power.

Proverbs 29:4.title: Proverbs 29:4
Proverbs 29:4.content: by judgment—that is, righteous decisions, opposed to those procured by gifts (compare Pr 28:21), by which good government is perverted. land—for nation.

Proverbs 29:5.title: Proverbs 29:5
Proverbs 29:5.content: (Compare Pr 26:28). spreadeth … feet—By misleading him as to his real character, the flatterer brings him to evil, prepared by himself or others.

Proverbs 29:6.title: Proverbs 29:6
Proverbs 29:6.content: In—or, "By" the transgression—he is brought into difficulty (Pr 12:13), but the righteous go on prospering, and so sing or rejoice.

Proverbs 29:7.title: Proverbs 29:7
Proverbs 29:7.content: considereth—literally, "knows," as Ps 1:6. the cause—that is, in courts of justice (compare Pr 29:14). The voluntary neglect of it by the wicked (Pr 28:27) occasions oppression.

Proverbs 29:8.title: Proverbs 29:8
Proverbs 29:8.content: Scornful men—those who contemptuously disregard God's law. bring—(Compare Margin), kindle strife. turn away wrath—that is, "abate wrath."

Proverbs 29:9.title: Proverbs 29:9
Proverbs 29:9.content: contendeth—that is, in law. whether … laugh—The fool, whether angry or good-humored, is unsettled; or referring the words to the wise man, the sense is, that all his efforts, severe or gentle, are unavailing to pacify the fool.

Proverbs 29:10.title: Proverbs 29:10
Proverbs 29:10.content: bloodthirsty—(Compare Margin), murderers (Ps 5:6; 26:9). hate, &c.—(Pr 1:11; Ge 3:4). seek … soul—that is, to preserve it.

Proverbs 29:11.title: Proverbs 29:11
Proverbs 29:11.content: (Compare Pr 12:16; 16:32). mind—or, "spirit," for anger or any ill passion which the righteous restrain.

Proverbs 29:13.title: Proverbs 29:13
Proverbs 29:13.content: (Compare Pr 22:2). deceitful man—literally, "man of vexations," an exactor. the Lord … their eyes—sustains their lives (1Sa 14:27; Ps 13:3); that is, both depend on Him, and He will do justice.

Proverbs 29:14.title: Proverbs 29:14
Proverbs 29:14.content: (Compare Pr 20:28; 25:5). Such is the character of the King of kings (Ps 72:4, 12).

Proverbs 29:16.title: Proverbs 29:16
Proverbs 29:16.content: (Compare Pr 29:2, 12; Ps 12:1-8). shall see … fall—and triumph in it (Ps 37:34-38; 58:10, 11).

Proverbs 29:17.title: Proverbs 29:17
Proverbs 29:17.content: (Compare Pr 29:3, 15; Pr 19:18). give thee rest—peace and quiet (compare Pr 29:9).

Proverbs 29:18.title: Proverbs 29:18
Proverbs 29:18.content: no vision—instruction in God's truth, which was by prophets, through visions (1Sa 3:1). people perish—(Compare Margin), are deprived of moral restraints. keepeth the law—has, and observes, instruction (Pr 14:11, 34; Ps 19:11).

Proverbs 29:19.title: Proverbs 29:19
Proverbs 29:19.content: A servant—who lacks good principle. corrected—or discovered. will not answer—that is, will not obey.

Proverbs 29:21.title: Proverbs 29:21
Proverbs 29:21.content: become his son—assume the place and privileges of one.

Proverbs 29:22.title: Proverbs 29:22
Proverbs 29:22.content: (Compare Pr 15:18). Such are delighted by discord and violence.

Proverbs 29:23.title: Proverbs 29:23
Proverbs 29:23.content: (Compare Pr 16:18; 18:12). honour … spirit—or, "such shall lay hold on honor" (Pr 11:16).

Proverbs 29:24.title: Proverbs 29:24
Proverbs 29:24.content: hateth … soul—(Compare Pr 8:36). heareth cursing—(Le 5:1), risks the punishment, rather than reveal truth.

Proverbs 29:25.title: Proverbs 29:25
Proverbs 29:25.content: The fear … snare—involves men in difficulty (compare Pr 29:6). shall be safe—(Compare Margin; Pr 18:10).

Proverbs 29:26.title: Proverbs 29:26
Proverbs 29:26.content: (Compare Margin; Ps 27:8). God alone will and can do exact justice.

Proverbs 29:27.title: Proverbs 29:27
Proverbs 29:27.content: (Compare Pr 3:32). On last clause, compare Pr 29:16; Ps 37:12.

Proverbs 30:1.title: Proverbs 30:1
Proverbs 30:1.content: This is the title of this chapter (see Introduction). the prophecy—literally, "the burden" (compare Isa 13:1; Zec 9:1), used for any divine instruction; not necessarily a prediction, which was only a kind of prophecy (1Ch 15:27, "a song"). Prophets were inspired men, who spoke for God to man, or for man to God (Ge 20:7; Ex 7:14, 15, 16). Such, also, were the New Testament prophets. In a general sense, Gad, Nathan, and others were such, who were divine teachers, though we do not learn that they ever predicted. the man spake—literally, "the saying of the man"; an expression used to denote any solemn and important announcement (compare 2Sa 23:1; Ps 36:1; 110:1; Isa 1:24, &c.). Ithiel and Ucal were perhaps pupils.

Proverbs 30:2.title: Proverbs 30:2-4
Proverbs 30:2.content: brutish—stupid, a strong term to denote his lowly self-estimation; or he may speak of such as his natural condition, as contrasted with God's all-seeing comprehensive knowledge and almighty power. The questions of this clause emphatically deny the attributes mentioned to be those of any creature, thus impressively strengthening the implied reference of the former to God (compare De 30:12-14; Isa 40:12; Eph 4:8).

Proverbs 30:3.title: Proverbs 30:2-4
Proverbs 30:3.content: brutish—stupid, a strong term to denote his lowly self-estimation; or he may speak of such as his natural condition, as contrasted with God's all-seeing comprehensive knowledge and almighty power. The questions of this clause emphatically deny the attributes mentioned to be those of any creature, thus impressively strengthening the implied reference of the former to God (compare De 30:12-14; Isa 40:12; Eph 4:8).

Proverbs 30:4.title: Proverbs 30:2-4
Proverbs 30:4.content: brutish—stupid, a strong term to denote his lowly self-estimation; or he may speak of such as his natural condition, as contrasted with God's all-seeing comprehensive knowledge and almighty power. The questions of this clause emphatically deny the attributes mentioned to be those of any creature, thus impressively strengthening the implied reference of the former to God (compare De 30:12-14; Isa 40:12; Eph 4:8).

Proverbs 30:6.title: Proverbs 30:6
Proverbs 30:6.content: Add … words—implying that his sole reliance was on God's all-sufficient teaching. reprove thee—or, "convict thee"—and so the falsehood will appear.

Proverbs 30:7.title: Proverbs 30:7-9
Proverbs 30:7.content: A prayer for exemption from wickedness, and the extremes of poverty and riches, the two things mentioned. Contentment is implied as desired.

Proverbs 30:8.title: Proverbs 30:7-9
Proverbs 30:8.content: A prayer for exemption from wickedness, and the extremes of poverty and riches, the two things mentioned. Contentment is implied as desired.

Proverbs 30:8.title: Proverbs 30:8
Proverbs 30:8.content: vanity—all sorts of sinful acts (Job 11:11; Isa 5:18).

Proverbs 30:9.title: Proverbs 30:7-9
Proverbs 30:9.content: A prayer for exemption from wickedness, and the extremes of poverty and riches, the two things mentioned. Contentment is implied as desired.

Proverbs 30:9.title: Proverbs 30:9
Proverbs 30:9.content: be full … deny—that is, puffed up by the pride of prosperity. take the name … vain—This is not (Hebrew) the form (compare Ex 20:7), but "take" rather denotes laying violent hold on any thing; that is, lest I assail God's name or attributes, as justice, mercy, &c., which the poor are tempted to do.

Proverbs 30:10.title: Proverbs 30:10
Proverbs 30:10.content: Accuse not—Slander not (Ps 10:7). curse … guilty—lest, however lowly, he be exasperated to turn on thee, and your guilt be made to appear.

Proverbs 30:11.title: Proverbs 30:11-14
Proverbs 30:11.content: Four kinds of hateful persons—(1) graceless children, (2) hypocrites, (3) the proud, (4) cruel oppressors (compare on Pr 30:14; Ps 14:4; 52:2)—are now illustrated; (1) Pr 30:15, 16, the insatiability of prodigal children and their fate; (2) Pr 30:17, hypocrisy, or the concealment of real character; (3 and 4) Pr 30:18-20, various examples of pride and oppression.

Proverbs 30:12.title: Proverbs 30:11-14
Proverbs 30:12.content: Four kinds of hateful persons—(1) graceless children, (2) hypocrites, (3) the proud, (4) cruel oppressors (compare on Pr 30:14; Ps 14:4; 52:2)—are now illustrated; (1) Pr 30:15, 16, the insatiability of prodigal children and their fate; (2) Pr 30:17, hypocrisy, or the concealment of real character; (3 and 4) Pr 30:18-20, various examples of pride and oppression.

Proverbs 30:13.title: Proverbs 30:11-14
Proverbs 30:13.content: Four kinds of hateful persons—(1) graceless children, (2) hypocrites, (3) the proud, (4) cruel oppressors (compare on Pr 30:14; Ps 14:4; 52:2)—are now illustrated; (1) Pr 30:15, 16, the insatiability of prodigal children and their fate; (2) Pr 30:17, hypocrisy, or the concealment of real character; (3 and 4) Pr 30:18-20, various examples of pride and oppression.

Proverbs 30:14.title: Proverbs 30:11-14
Proverbs 30:14.content: Four kinds of hateful persons—(1) graceless children, (2) hypocrites, (3) the proud, (4) cruel oppressors (compare on Pr 30:14; Ps 14:4; 52:2)—are now illustrated; (1) Pr 30:15, 16, the insatiability of prodigal children and their fate; (2) Pr 30:17, hypocrisy, or the concealment of real character; (3 and 4) Pr 30:18-20, various examples of pride and oppression.

Proverbs 30:15.title: Proverbs 30:15-16
Proverbs 30:15.content: horse leech—supposed by some to be the vampire (a fabulous creature), as being literally insatiable; but the other subjects mentioned must be taken as this, comparatively insatiable. The use of a fabulous creature agreeably to popular notions is not inconsistent with inspiration. There are three … yea, four—(Compare Pr 6:16).

Proverbs 30:16.title: Proverbs 30:15-16
Proverbs 30:16.content: horse leech—supposed by some to be the vampire (a fabulous creature), as being literally insatiable; but the other subjects mentioned must be taken as this, comparatively insatiable. The use of a fabulous creature agreeably to popular notions is not inconsistent with inspiration. There are three … yea, four—(Compare Pr 6:16).

Proverbs 30:17.title: Proverbs 30:17
Proverbs 30:17.content: The eye—for the person, with reference to the use of the organ to express mockery and contempt, and also as that by which punishment is received. the ravens … eagles … eat—either as dying unnaturally, or being left unburied, or both.

Proverbs 30:18.title: Proverbs 30:18-20
